Jane (Acme): Hey team — after upgrading to py-sdk 0.12.1 our rerank responses are all zeros for score. Sent 50 candidates, got back 0.0 for everything. Tried with curl (raw API) and works fine.

Mike - Support: ugh, sorry you're blocked. Can you paste the exact request payload you sent (sanitized) and the SDK call? Also which model/rerank endpoint?

Jane (Acme): Using /v1/rerank, model=rdrwk/rerank-v1. Payload (sanitized):
```json
{"query": "best support ticket", "candidates": [{"id":"c1","text":"...","score":"0.0"}, {"id":"c2","text":"...","score":"0.0"} ...] }
```
Note the SDK call was: `client.rerank(query, candidates)` from py-sdk.

Paul - SDK: thanks — that payload is the clue. Looks like the Python SDK is serializing score as strings ("0.0"). The server expects numeric fields; when strings arrive the comparator path falls back and yields 0.0 effectively. Can you paste the snippet you use to build candidates?

Jane (Acme): sure —
```py
candidates = []
for c in raw:
    candidates.append({"id": c.id, "text": c.text, "score": str(c.confidence)})  # we were coercing to str earlier for logging
client.rerank(query=query, candidates=candidates)
```

Mike - Support: ahah, that explains it — you were converting to string in your app code. But we also saw a few other customers with 0.0 who didn't do that. Could be SDK doing additional coercion in some edge cases.

Paul - SDK: I can repro with a small harness. There's also a separate TypeScript SDK issue where candidate arrays can get re-ordered when the caller passes a plain Array of objects with prototypes — we mutated objects while attaching metadata. That can change mapping between candidate id and score. TL;DR: two separate bugs seen in wild: Python string-serialize and TS mutation/order bug.

Alyssa - EngML: from model side, we treat score as float and assume proper numeric JSON. If it sees strings we attempt parseFloat but fallback logic causes ties to be treated as zero in ranking comparator for safety. So both bugs cause weird rank results.

Jane (Acme): ok — what's the remediation path? We have production traffic.

Paul - SDK: immediate workaround: ensure your app sends numeric types (remove str() around confidence). We will push a hotfix to py-sdk to validate candidate fields and cast numeric-looking strings to floats before sending. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/432 (draft). Hotfix ETA ~3 hrs.

Paul - SDK: for TS users, avoid in-place mutation; map candidates with `candidates.map(c => ({...c}))` before passing to `rerank`. We'll release TS patch EOD. PR for TS: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/217

Mike - Support: I'll mark this as P2 -> escalate to SDK team. Also opening a small server-side leniency change to accept numeric-strings more gracefully for a short period so customers aren't immediately broken. Ops will coordinate.

Jane (Acme): thanks, please confirm when hotfix is out. Would also like a rollback-safe mitigation if we can't patch quick.

Paul - SDK: will post here when 0.12.2 published and when TS patch lands. In the meantime, if you can run a quick script to coerce candidate scores to numbers before calling, that'll restore behavior. Example: `c.score = Number(c.score)` in JS or `float(c['score'])` in Python.

ci-bot: deploy queued: py-sdk/0.12.2-hotfix -> staging (build 184).

Mike - Support: following up with Jane once hotfix is validated. Thanks everyone for quick triage. :thumbsup:
